aliases: wound botulism from injection drug use
gold.reasoning: 1. Guillain–Barré syndrome considered — “Guillain-Barré syndrome is an autoimmune disease that demyelinates neurons and causes an ascending paralysis.” 2. Miller Fisher variant of Guillain–Barré syndrome considered — “However, the Miller Fischer variant of Guillain-Barré syndrome presents with a descending paralysis, closer mimicking that of botulism.” 3. Myasthenia gravis considered — “Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune neuromuscular disease that results in weakness of certain muscle groups, sometimes including facial and respiratory muscles.” 4. Brainstem stroke considered — “Bilateral or brainstem strokes can also cause similar symptoms such as facial drooping, limb weakness, and breathing difficulties.” 5. Wound botulism favored — “Therefore, the suspicion was for possible wound botulism.”

Signs the patient can notice (drooping eyelids, double vision, slurred speech, saliva pooling, head drop, arm weakness, abscesses) are facts in lay words and also stay in the examination findings.
